issues.description: default_response_to_output_transformer can raise on non-JSON lines, aborting the stream mid-response
issues.detail: json.loads is called inside the per-line loop with no try/except. A single malformed SSE line (heartbeat, comment, partial chunk) raises JSONDecodeError and propagates out of process_frame, leaving _output_response_open True and the LLMFullResponseEndFrame unsent. The invariant 'every Start has a matching End' is not preserved on the exception path.

issues.description: SSE parsing is not RFC-compliant: hardcoded 6-char slice and naive split('\n') mishandle \r\n, fields, and event boundaries
issues.detail: SSE frames are delimited by blank lines and may carry id:, event:, retry:, or comments (lines starting with ':'). The code only recognizes 'data: ' with a fixed offset of 6, warns on everything else, and splits on '\n' so '\r\n' transports leave stray CRs. State the invariant or use an SSE parser; the current loop is asymptotically O(N) but practically wrong on conforming servers.

issues.description: Client is reconstructed per LLMContextFrame, paying TLS+auth setup cost on every turn
issues.detail: async with self._aws_session.client(...) inside process_frame creates a new bedrock-agentcore client for every invocation. For a streaming conversational loop this is the hot path; the constant factor here is large (handshake, credential resolution). Cache the client in setup()/start() and reuse it. This is the 3% worth optimizing because it is per-turn latency the user feels.

issues.description: agentArn parameter name violates PEP 8 and the surrounding API's snake_case convention
issues.detail: Every other constructor argument uses snake_case (aws_access_key, aws_region). agentArn is camelCase and is also stored as self._agentArn. Readers will trip on this; a reader is the constraint. Rename to agent_arn (and _agent_arn) before this ships, since renaming a public kwarg later is a breaking change.

issues.description: Timeout-close invariant is not stated and races with the final close in process_frame
issues.detail: _close_output_response_after_timeout flips _output_response_open and emits End, while the tail of process_frame also cancels the task and emits End. The intended invariant ('exactly one End per Start') holds in the common case but depends on cancel_task semantics and event-loop ordering. State the invariant in a comment and consider a single close helper to make termination obvious.

issues.description: default_context_to_payload_transformer silently truncates multimodal content parts
issues.detail: When content is a list, it joins part.get('text', '') across all parts. Image or tool-result parts contribute empty strings, producing a payload of stray spaces with no warning. Either filter to text parts explicitly or log when non-text parts are dropped, so the contract ('latest user/system text') is honest.

review.summary: The processor is straightforward and mostly readable, but it is UNDER-AUDITED on two fronts: the SSE parser's invariants are not stated and do not match the spec (fixed 'data: ' offset, naive newline split, no CR handling, no try/except around json.loads), and the bookend invariant 'every LLMFullResponseStartFrame has exactly one matching EndFrame' is not preserved on exception paths. Performance has one real 3%: the bedrock-agentcore client is rebuilt per turn, which is the kind of constant-factor cost a profiler would flag immediately. Naming (agentArn) breaks the surrounding snake_case convention and should be fixed before the API is public. Verdict: UNDER-AUDITED, with a side of NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT around the streaming state machine.
